# Object macros in expanded field positions

All ten isolated projects in `cases/` match Joern v4.0.555 across the complete selected AST/NODES/EDGES/FLOWS projection: 2,366 canonical lines including method separators. The frozen fourth-checkpoint production binary matched three cases; seven failed before this increment. The regression test builds each case through `Project`, `CFrontend`, and the standard analysis pipeline, then compares the entire canonical dump.

Tree-sitter identifies a token after `.` or `->` as `field_identifier`. The existing macro-body renderer expanded only `identifier` and `type_identifier`, leaving object macros such as `Len` and `Code` unchanged in generated expression and statement bodies. The repair includes field tokens in the same object-macro lookup, using its existing disabled-macro set and work budget. Function-like macro names without arguments remain unchanged.

The conformant cases pin scalar field aliases, object alias chains, nesting through a function-like macro, array receivers, a field replacement containing a subscript, statement assignments, and source-order redefinition. Self-recursion, a function-like name used as a field, and an unrelated field retain their previously exact output. No type registry, cast parser, CFG, or reaching-definition solver code changes.

`diagnostics/` retains the initial eight complete exploratory graphs, before/candidate outputs, and full differences. Their valid named nested-struct declarations expose existing TYPE scaffold differences even in `nonfield`, which uses no field macro. The nested, alias and array macro AST field differences are repaired, while those scaffold differences remain. Direct `p->Len` and `item.Len` still require separate lowering: Joern emits the expanded field structure while preserving the original access CODE on generated calls. That direct path is being investigated separately; this increment does not claim it is repaired. Two exploratory negative cases are already exact. No diagnostic graph facts are filtered out.

The unchanged 26-file zlib input was also replayed. `_tr_align` has no remaining `FIELD_IDENTIFIER Len/Code` nodes (three before), and `compress_block` has none (twelve before). Their complete method ASTs and remaining diffs are retained in `evidence/`; neither method nor the whole project is exact because cast/type differences remain. `measurement.json` binds the unchanged input manifest and complete whole-project raw outputs, retained locally, as well as these method extracts. The debug replay is correctness evidence, not a performance benchmark.

The two `oracle/` directories retain raw stdout, stderr, invocation metadata and scripts. Each script uses the unchanged shared `oracle.sc` projection with a driver that imports one isolated directory per distinct Joern project. To regenerate, run the focused script against `cases/` in a fresh scratch working directory with the pinned Joern installation and JDK 21.0.12. Remove only the `AST|` transport prefix when extracting each `CASE|` section. Existing newline transport is noninjective and unchanged; expected output must not be edited by hand.

The measurement binds source, binary, reference and raw-output hashes, including the frozen baseline `862e54ee5` source. Validation logs cover the new production regression, the relevant Rust suites, formatting, strict Clippy and the existing 308-block committed/live gate. Historical baseline files remain unchanged.
